title: 高龄的人如何与邻居搞好关系?
desc: 高龄的人如何与邻居搞好关系?

paragraphs.en: I am 86 and have been on my own for many years. However, despite being financially secure, it is a lonely life and I realise I've fallen into a materially comfortable rut.
paragraphs.zh: 我今年86岁，多年来一直独自生活。然而，尽管经济上有保障，这种生活却十分孤独，我意识到自己已陷入了物质舒适却单调乏味的生活状态。

paragraphs.en: Come 6pm I eat a meal, usually microwaved, have a shower, put my PJs on, lock the doors, put the TV on and settle down to another boring evening.
paragraphs.zh: 每到傍晚六点，我吃一顿通常是微波加热的饭，洗个澡，换上睡衣，锁好门，打开电视，然后开始又一个乏味的夜晚。

paragraphs.en: My children live far away and have their own lives, although I do encourage them to visit me as much as they can and my grandchildren do, for the occasional weekend.
paragraphs.zh: 我的孩子们住得很远，各有各的生活，虽然我确实鼓励他们尽可能多来看我，我的孙辈们偶尔也会来过周末。

paragraphs.en: Sometimes, though, I can go days without talking to anyone.
paragraphs.zh: 但有时候，我可能连续几天都没个人说话。

paragraphs.en: I used to belong to several singles groups but Covid caused them to close and not reopen again.
paragraphs.zh: 我曾经加入过几个单身人士团体，但新冠疫情导致这些团体关闭且未能重新开放。

paragraphs.en: I am in reasonably good health, although walking any distance is a problem now.
paragraphs.zh: 我的健康状况还算不错，尽管现在走远路有些困难。

paragraphs.en: My question is: there's a nice lady, a little younger than myself, who lives next door and we have chats over the fence.
paragraphs.zh: 我的问题是：隔壁住着一位很不错的女士，比我稍年轻些，我们常隔着篱笆聊天。

paragraphs.en: I would love to know her better and think she feels the same, but I feel if I asked her out for a coffee away from our homes but got a rebuff, it could spoil our current friendship. Any advice?
paragraphs.zh: 我很想更深入地了解她，也觉得她可能有同样的想法，但我担心如果我邀请她到外面去喝杯咖啡，却遭到拒绝，可能会破坏我们现有的友谊。有什么建议吗？

paragraphs.en: Eleanor says: I think the best advice I ever got for getting closer to people is to act like you already are.
paragraphs.zh: 埃莉诺说：我认为我得到过的关于拉近与他人距离的最佳建议是，表现得好像你们已经关系很亲近了。

paragraphs.en: Not in a creepy way, obviously – I don't mean you ask personal questions or presume you're invited without being asked.
paragraphs.zh: 当然不是以令人不适的方式——我并不是说你要问私人问题，或者未经邀请就假定自己得到了邀请。

paragraphs.en: I just mean, you suggest doing something together as though you already do things together.
paragraphs.zh: 我的意思是，你可以提议一起做点什么，就好像你们已经经常一起做事一样。

paragraphs.en: I'm not sure whether your hope for taking the friendship further is romantic or platonic, but this idea could apply to either circumstance.
paragraphs.zh: 我不确定你希望将友谊推向更深层次是出于浪漫还是柏拉图式的情感，但这个想法对两种情况都适用。

paragraphs.en: That awkward stiffness we sometimes feel when we try to progress a relationship one notch closer – I think that's both people feeling they don't quite know the rules of the new, closer interaction.
paragraphs.zh: 当我们试图让一段关系更进一步时，那种尴尬的拘谨感——我想这源于双方都觉得自己不太清楚这种更亲密互动的新规则。

paragraphs.en: It could be asking a colleague out socially, a group friend for a one-on-one outing, or an acquaintance to do something more romantic.
paragraphs.zh: 这可能是邀请同事进行社交活动、约群里的朋友单独出去游玩，或者约一个熟人开展更浪漫的活动。

paragraphs.en: There's always that first moment in new territory – oh, we do this together now? If the primary feeling in that moment is that it's new, it can kind of judder the existing relationship.
paragraphs.zh: 踏入新领域时总会有那样的第一刻——哦，我们现在要一起做这个了吗？如果那一刻的主要感受是一切都是新的，那么这可能会对现有的关系造成一些冲击。

paragraphs.en: If instead, you extend the invitation with the ease you'd have talking to someone you know well, it feels more like you've been close all along.
paragraphs.zh: 相反，如果你能像和熟人交谈那样轻松地发出邀请，就会让人感觉你们一直都很亲密。

paragraphs.en: "Fancy a cup of tea?", easy as you like, a canoe gliding off the bank.
paragraphs.zh: “想喝杯茶吗？”，轻松随意，就像独木舟悠然离岸。

paragraphs.en: The second-best advice I ever got was to do things that aren't sitting on opposite sides of a restaurant table looking at each other.
paragraphs.zh: 我得到过的第二好的建议是，不要只是坐在餐厅的桌子两边，面对面干坐着。

paragraphs.en: It's easier to get to know someone if we find things to do together that aren't just being together.
paragraphs.zh: 如果我们能一起做些事情，而不只是单纯待在一起，就更容易了解一个人。

paragraphs.en: Does anything need potting? Is there a little practical problem you've talked about that you could offer to solve, a game or puzzle you've mentioned, a shared interest that connects to an exhibition or a book event or concert you'd like to go to, a skill she has that you want to learn (or vice versa) such that one of you could teach the other?
paragraphs.zh: 有什么需要栽种的东西吗？你们之前提到过的一个小小的实际问题，你能不能主动帮忙解决；你提到过的一个游戏或谜题；一种共同的兴趣，它与一场展览、一场图书活动或一场音乐会相关，而你想去参加；她掌握的一项技能，你想学（或者反过来，你掌握的技能她想学），这样你们其中一人就可以教另一人。

paragraphs.en: Perhaps you simply have too much cake in the house and need someone to share the burden of eating it.
paragraphs.zh: 也许只是你家里蛋糕太多了，需要有人一起分担吃掉它。

paragraphs.en: The advantage of that sort of thing is it feels like an extension of your existing relationship rather than a change to a new one.
paragraphs.zh: 这类事情的好处在于，它感觉像是你现有关系的延续，而非转变为一种新的关系。

paragraphs.en: If it doesn't go well, you can both de-escalate with plausible deniability.
paragraphs.zh: 如果进展不顺利，你们双方都可以以看似合理的借口缓和关系。

paragraphs.en: That's what I'd look for at first if I were you – ways to spend more time chatting that don't feel like big threshold-crossing moments.
paragraphs.zh: 如果我是你，一开始我会寻找这样的方式——能让你们有更多时间聊天，且不会让人觉得是会有重大突破的方式。

paragraphs.en: I was reading some dating advice from the 1930s recently, expecting to laugh a bit, and was duly humbled by the fact that many suggestions were totally evergreen.
paragraphs.zh: 最近，我读了一些20世纪30年代的约会建议，本想着能乐一乐，结果却因许多建议完全不过时这一事实而深感惭愧。

paragraphs.en: In particular, everybody said they wanted someone "of good cheer".
paragraphs.zh: 特别是，人人都说他们想找一个“开朗乐观”的人。

paragraphs.en: Vim and laughter are such good fuel for any kind of companionship. Cheerful foot forwards. Leave any slightly lonely feet at home.
paragraphs.zh: 活力和欢笑是任何一种陪伴关系的绝佳动力。带着欢快的步伐向前迈进，把那些略带孤独的情绪留在家里。

paragraphs.en: There are many fun ways to get to know each other that will be absorbing, warm and entertaining, long before proffering a formal invitation that could be rejected.
paragraphs.zh: 在发出可能会被拒绝的正式邀请之前，有很多有趣的方式可以让彼此相互了解，这些方式既引人入胜，又温馨有趣。

paragraphs.en: Indeed, these little steps may be the best path to her wanting to accept such an invitation when it comes.
paragraphs.zh: 实际上，在正式邀请到来之前，这些小步骤可能是让她愿意接受邀请的最佳途径。
